drivingQuestion: How can Rav Huna's requirement to distance oneself from feces before him as far as the eye sees be reconciled with Rav Ḥisda's permission to stand opposite a bathroom and pray?
outcomeNote: Reconciled by oqimta: Rav Ḥisda's permission concerns a newly built, unused bathroom, and Ravina's dilemma about designation concerned praying inside it, not opposite it. Rava adds that Persian bathrooms count as sealed.

segments.he: אִינִי?! וְהָא אָמַר רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: עוֹמֵד אָדָם כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית הַכִּסֵּא וּמִתְפַּלֵּל! הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? בְּבֵית הַכִּסֵּא שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ צוֹאָה.
segments.en: The Gemara challenges this: «Is that so? Didn’t Rafram bar Pappa say» that «Rav Ḥisda said: One may stand opposite a bathroom and pray.» The Gemara resolves this contradiction: «With what are we dealing here? With a bathroom that has no feces,» and therefore there is no need to distance himself to that extent.

segments.he: אִינִי?! וְהָאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חֲנִינָא: בֵּית הַכִּסֵּא שֶׁאָמְרוּ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ צוֹאָה וּבֵית הַמֶּרְחָץ שֶׁאָמְרוּ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אָדָם! אֶלָּא הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן — בְּחַדְתֵי.
segments.en: The Gemara asks again: «Is that so? Didn’t Rav Yosef bar Ḥanina say: The bathroom to which» the Sages «referred» in all of the halakhot of distancing oneself was «even» one «in which there were no feces, and the bathhouse to which» the Sages «referred» in all of the halakhot of uttering sacred matters, was «even» one «in which there was no» naked «person. Rather, with what are we dealing here?» We are dealing «with a new» structure, built as a bathroom but not yet used for that purpose.

segments.he: וְהָא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְרָבִינָא: הִזְמִינוֹ לְבֵית הַכִּסֵּא, מַהוּ? יֵשׁ זִימּוּן, אוֹ אֵין זִימּוּן? כִּי קָא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְרָבִינָא: לְמֵיקַם עֲלֵיהּ לְצַלּוֹיֵי בְּגַוֵּיהּ אֲבָל כְּנֶגְדּוֹ — לָא.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «Wasn’t this» already «raised as a dilemma» by «Ravina: One who designated» the structure for use «as a bathroom, what is its» legal status? Is «designation» effective «or is designation not» effective? The Gemara replies: «When Ravina raised the dilemma,» it was whether or not one may «stand and pray inside it, but» he had «no» dilemma whether or «not one may pray opposite it.»

segments.he: אָמַר רָבָא: הָנֵי בָּתֵּי כִּסָּאֵי דְּפָרְסָאֵי אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִית בְּהוּ צוֹאָה — כִּסְתוּמִין דָּמוּ.
segments.en: «Rava said: These Persian bathrooms, even though they contain feces, they are considered as sealed,» as they are constructed on an incline so the feces will roll out of the bathroom underground.

moves.cueHe: איני?! והא אמר רפרם בר פפא אמר רב חסדא
moves.summary: The stam objects to Rav Huna's ruling (previous unit) from Rav Ḥisda's dictum, via Rafram bar Pappa, that one may stand opposite a bathroom and pray.
moves.about: whether one must distance himself from feces before him as far as the eye sees, given that Rav Ḥisda permits standing opposite a bathroom and praying

moves.cueHe: הכא במאי עסקינן? בבית הכסא שאין בו צואה
moves.summary: Oqimta: Rav Ḥisda speaks of a bathroom containing no feces.
moves.about: Rav Ḥisda's dictum (reported by Rafram bar Pappa) that one may stand opposite a bathroom and pray, adduced against Rav Huna

moves.cueHe: איני?! והאמר רב יוסף בר חנינא
moves.summary: The stam attacks that oqimta from Rav Yosef bar Ḥanina: the 'bathroom' of the Sages' rulings is even one without feces (and the 'bathhouse' even one without a person).
moves.about: whether Rav Ḥisda's 'bathroom' can be one without feces, given Rav Yosef bar Ḥanina's dictum that the bathroom the Sages spoke of is even one containing no feces

moves.summary: Revised oqimta: Rav Ḥisda speaks of a new bathroom, built but never used.
moves.about: Rav Yosef bar Ḥanina's dictum that 'bathroom' and 'bathhouse' in the Sages' rulings include one without feces and one without a person

moves.summary: The stam objects: Ravina left it as an open dilemma whether designating a structure as a bathroom takes effect, so a new bathroom cannot simply be permitted.
moves.about: whether a new, unused bathroom can simply be permitted, since Ravina raised as an open dilemma whether designating a structure as a bathroom takes effect

moves.summary: Ravina's dilemma concerned praying inside the designated bathroom; praying opposite it was no dilemma for him.
moves.about: Ravina's dilemma about designation of a bathroom, adduced against the 'new bathroom' answer

moves.cueHe: אמר רבא: הני בתי כסאי דפרסאי
moves.summary: Rava: Persian bathrooms, even though they contain feces, are treated as sealed.
